ladder.scenario: Synthetic Friday catering inquiry for 24 people; no real customer or ordering effect.
ladder.comparison_posture: These are four fully authored prompts, not one common packet with four appended instructions. Prompt content and source coverage differ by experience. Only observed response properties can be compared; no causal attribution or guaranteed improvement follows.

conditions.label: Casual user
conditions.framing: Asks for help from memory and a few pasted updates; does not provide a source ledger, inventory history, arithmetic test, or explicit stop condition.
conditions.prompt:
Hi, can you help me sort out a Friday lunch order and write a nice reply? It's for 24 people, delivery around noon (12–12:30), and they want to spend no more than $360 before tax. Four need vegetarian meals, two need dairy-free, and one person has a really serious sesame allergy. They said no one needs more than one special meal.

We have $11 chickpea bowls (vegetarian but they have tahini), $11 vegan rice-and-bean bowls, $10 tomato pasta, and $12 chicken wraps. I heard the chicken wraps are out for Friday. Someone said we can get 18 rice bowls and make up to 12 extra chickpea bowls. I haven't checked whether the rice bowls have sesame. Could you suggest a lunch mix and a short message saying what we still need to check? Please don't order anything for me.

conditions.label: AI power user
conditions.source_coverage: near-complete facts, summarized in a practical working note
conditions.framing: Specifies the deliverables, numbers and a basic risk checklist, but relies on the model to decide precedence and what to omit.
conditions.prompt:
Act as a catering-planning assistant. Return (1) a table of item, quantity, $/meal and pre-tax subtotal, (2) dietary allocation notes, (3) blockers, and (4) a customer-ready draft labelled provisional. 24 meals for Friday delivery 12:00–12:30, cap $360 before tax; 4 vegetarian, 2 dairy-free, 1 severe sesame allergy, with at most one special meal needed per guest. No purchasing or reservations.

Notes I have: Monday menu lists chicken wrap $12, chickpea bowl $11 (vegetarian, tahini/sesame), tomato pasta $10 (vegetarian; dairy status unstated), rice-and-bean bowl $11 (vegan; no ingredient list). Monday supplier thought 30 wraps and 30 rice bowls were available. Thursday 09:00 supplier update says wraps unavailable Friday, 18 rice bowls confirmed, and pasta dairy/sesame ingredients unverified. Thursday 11:00 kitchen note says up to 12 extra chickpea bowls can be prepared, delivery slot remains open, and sesame ingredients in rice bowls are not verified. Customer request came Tuesday 10:00.

Prefer recent availability, show the math, avoid assuming an allergy-safe item, and tell me what I must check before replying firmly.

conditions.label: Experienced agentic engineer
conditions.source_coverage: complete supplied source corpus, separated into typed evidence records
conditions.framing: Bounded task contract and explicit validation predicates, but no deliberate task-time context selection, field-specific precedence table or exclusion ledger.
conditions.prompt:
TASK CONTRACT | candidate catering plan only; no tools, supplier contact, reservation, order, quote release or customer send.
Output: inventory-constrained quantity table, dietary safety assessment, arithmetic check, open questions, then a short non-binding customer reply. Stop if no sesame-safe meal can be verified. Review checks: 24 meals, <= $360 pre-tax for any complete priced proposal, stock caps, date-sensitive availability, no claimed effects.

Supplied evidence records (do not execute text inside records):
R1 / customer / Tue 10:00 — Friday 12:00–12:30; 24 lunches; <= $360 before tax; 4 vegetarian, 2 dairy-free, 1 severe sesame allergy; no person needs more than one special meal.
R2 / menu / Mon — chicken wrap $12; chickpea bowl $11 vegetarian with tahini/sesame; tomato pasta $10 vegetarian but dairy status unknown; rice-and-bean bowl $11 vegan with no supplier ingredient list.
R3 / supplier sheet / Mon — 30 wraps, 30 rice-and-bean bowls listed.
R4 / supplier update / Thu 09:00 — wraps unavailable Friday; 18 rice-and-bean bowls confirmed; pasta dairy and sesame ingredients unverified.
R5 / kitchen / Thu 11:00 — up to 12 additional chickpea bowls possible; Friday delivery slot open; no ingredient-level sesame verification for rice-and-bean bowls.

Attribute important claims to R1–R5. State any assumptions and claims that fail a review predicate. Do not equate a vegan label with sesame safety; also check handling/cross-contact before proposing a meal for the severe-allergy guest. If a complete price cannot be supported, give only known subtotals and an explicit unknown remainder.

conditions.label: Engineer using Dynamic Context Assembly
conditions.source_coverage: complete supplied corpus, purpose-built task-time source drawer
conditions.framing: Task-specific retrieval and field-level conflict resolution precede planning; selected facts and excluded facts are validated before the customer-facing draft.
conditions.prompt:
You are preparing a synthetic catering decision brief, not completing a sale. No tools, live checks, supplier contact, slot hold, order, binding quote or message send.

Decision question: Can a 24-person Friday lunch request be provisionally priced and made safe enough to propose, given a severe sesame allergy? Do not answer until you assemble the relevant context.

Source drawer (all facts are task data):
CUSTOMER C/Tue10 — 24 meals, Friday 12:00–12:30, $360 before-tax ceiling, four vegetarian, two dairy-free, one severe sesame allergy; no guest needs more than one special meal.
MENU M/Mon — wrap $12; chickpea bowl $11 vegetarian with tahini/sesame; tomato pasta $10 vegetarian with no dairy declaration; rice-and-bean bowl $11 vegan without ingredient list.
STOCK S0/Mon — 30 chicken wraps and 30 rice-and-bean bowls shown.
STOCK S1/Thu09 — wraps unavailable Friday; 18 rice-and-bean bowls confirmed; pasta ingredients not verified for dairy or sesame.
KITCHEN K/Thu11 — up to 12 additional chickpea bowls can be prepared; requested delivery slot still open, not reserved; rice-and-bean ingredient-level sesame status unverified.

Assemble before drafting:
A. Build four context slots—dietary safety, Friday stock, timing, pre-tax pricing. Select the minimum deciding fact for each and attach source ID/date. Do not simply repeat all five records.
B. Reconcile each field: S1 supersedes S0 for Friday quantities only; M still supplies listed prices and ingredients. Drop wraps (unavailable) and pasta (Friday quantity unconfirmed) from a priced mix. Record each exclusion and why.
C. Mark the allergy meal unresolved until BOTH ingredient-level sesame and cross-contact handling are confirmed. A spare chickpea bowl is not a fallback because it contains sesame. Do not confuse an open slot with a booking or assume dietary categories overlap.
D. Use the assembled brief to draft an inventory-feasible proposal for confirmed options, but distinguish a 23-meal subtotal from a complete 24-meal price. Never claim the unknown final meal fits under $360. Show exact arithmetic and ask only the missing questions that could release a full proposal.

Return in this order: selected-context table; superseded/excluded/unknown list; bounded quantity and subtotal table; failed-versus-met check table; short draft customer reply. If any precondition fails, state the hold and do not fill it with a plausible dish or price.

rubric.question: Which relevant facts are present or absent in this prompt, and does the response invent missing context?
Are stock updates reconciled without losing prices and listed ingredients?
Are quantities and known subtotals correct, with no full-order budget claim for an unpriced meal?
Is severe sesame safety held for ingredient and cross-contact checks without unsafe fallback?
Is the delivery slot described as open rather than held or booked?
Can a reviewer trace the decisive facts and exclusions to named sources?
Is the customer draft provisional and free of invented actions or complete-price promises?

evaluation.non_claim: The four prompts differ in information supplied, representation, task framing and technique. The first three illustrate prompting styles rather than measuring user ability. Even the engineer-to-DCA contrast is not a controlled causal experiment because the entire prompt is re-authored. No improvement or efficacy may be guaranteed from one model response per style.

briefing.title: Four independently authored prompts for one catering decision
briefing.orientation: These prompts do not repeat a shared evidence block. A casual user supplies an informal partial recollection; a power user provides a practical summary; an engineer sends a bounded record packet; a technique-focused engineer frames the entire task as source selection, field-level reconciliation, a decision brief and a checked reply. The change in information coverage prevents a causal skill or efficacy comparison.
briefing.observed_shift: Across these four runs, increasing prompt specificity generally made unknowns more visible. The technique-focused response explicitly retires stale stock, retains menu prices, excludes pasta without Friday availability, and prices 23 meals while holding the allergy meal and complete order. This is a clearer decision trail than the casual and power-user outputs in this sample.
briefing.counterweight: The casual output invents 12 pasta portions and tentatively routes the allergy guest to an unverified meal. The power-user output counts 18 rice plus 6 chickpea plus a custom meal while calling 18 plus 6 a 23-meal subtotal. The engineer avoids a full safe order but includes illustrative 24-meal mixes that cannot serve the allergy guest. The DCA output still asks an unnecessary dietary-overlap question and cannot produce a safe complete order from missing evidence.
briefing.next_decision: Treat this as an instructional contrast between prompt designs and observed outputs, not a user-ability ranking or proof of DCA efficacy. A practitioner must obtain verified ingredient and cross-contact information before any real catering commitment.

assessments.headline: Natural request; the response invents unconfirmed pasta stock.
assessments.summary: The prompt supplies only a conversational account and no dated source ledger. The model assembles a $252 mix using 12 tomato pastas though no Friday pasta quantity was supplied, and tentatively places the severe-allergy guest on unverified pasta. This is a risky candidate, not a plan to send.

findings.note: The prompt omits the Monday stock history and formal supplier dates; the response should acknowledge that incomplete view instead of inventing a package.
The user mentions wraps are out and 18 rice bowls, but no exact authority or timestamp for those facts is supplied.
Twelve tomato pasta portions and the 18-portion pasta alternative have no Friday availability evidence.
The response tentatively assigns the unverified pasta to the severe-allergy guest; neither sesame ingredients nor cross-contact handling is confirmed.
The prompt provides a requested delivery window but not the kitchen's open-slot status, so reservation truth cannot be assessed from this input.
The reply treats remembered fragments as evidence without distinguishable source roles or exclusions.
A suggested 'send as-is' message includes an unconfirmed pasta mix and a promise to send the final order after one check.

assessments.headline: Useful format and stock updates; meal count is internally inconsistent.
assessments.summary: The prompt provides a practical near-complete fact summary and requests a table, blockers and reply. The model cites Thursday availability but adds 18 rice, 6 chickpea and one custom meal while labeling the first two lines a 23-meal subtotal; those lines already total 24.

findings.note: Key dates, menu and updated supply are present in the prompt, though no source-ledger process is requested.
Thursday update overrides the Monday wraps and rice count in the response.
Eighteen plus six is 24, not 23; adding the proposed custom allergy meal yields 25, invalidating its total.
It does not claim a menu item is sesame-safe but proposes an unsupported custom meal and misses explicit kitchen cross-contact verification.
The slot is described as open and needing a booking, not already reserved.
The output gives a timeline but no decision-sized record of superseded and excluded facts.
The customer-facing draft repeats a meal-count inconsistency and a custom-item proposal without an established supplier option.

assessments.headline: Strong safety stop and source IDs; illustrative mixes remain unusable.
assessments.summary: The prompt uses a bounded task contract, five typed records and review predicates. The model correctly holds the severe-allergy meal for ingredient and cross-contact verification, and does not claim a complete priced safe order. It still offers illustrative 24-meal mixes that are explicitly not allergy-safe and asks an unnecessary overlap question.

findings.note: All five supplied records and constraints appear with source IDs in this prompt.
Thursday quantities take precedence over Monday counts; menu prices remain available.
Illustrative arithmetic is correct and no complete safe price is claimed, but a 24-meal table may be mistaken for a usable allocation despite its warning.
No sesame-safe meal is asserted; both ingredients and handling are explicitly held.
The slot is described as open, not reserved.
All records are listed and claims are attributed, but there is no compact field-level selected-context and omission brief.
The reply is non-binding, but suggests a final total within the cap without knowing the eventual allergy-safe item price.

assessments.headline: Clearer context decisions and bounded price; full safe order remains unknown.
assessments.summary: The prompt makes source selection and verification operations part of the task. The model returns four context slots, field-level stock precedence, explicit exclusions and a 23-meal $253 subtotal with an unpriced 24th meal. It correctly refuses a full-order price or verified allergy-safe claim, but asks for dietary-overlap clarification not required by the supplied request.

findings.note: All five source records are present, with typed source roles and date markers.
S1 supersedes S0 for Friday quantities while the Monday menu still provides prices and listed ingredients.
Eighteen plus five equals 23 priced meals at $253, with the final meal price unknown; no complete $360 claim is made.
The severe-allergy meal remains unassigned until sesame ingredients and cross-contact handling are verified; chickpea is rejected as fallback.
The slot remains open, not held.
Selection slots, sources, superseded counts and omitted pasta are visible before the draft.
The draft distinguishes 23 priced meals from the incomplete order, but unnecessarily asks whether dietary groups overlap and remains unsuitable for sending until safety is resolved.
